results.question: When do I send my first unemployment status report to Kela?
results.answer: In your first application, you report your unemployment dates starting from your first day of unemployment [S1]. To get your first benefit payment, you must submit an unemployment status report covering a 2-week period after submitting your first application [S1][S6]. For example, if you apply on 14 February, your first 2-week period ends on 27 February, meaning the first day you can submit your report is 28 February [S6]. If you cannot use the OmaKela e-service, you can mail a printed form [S2][S5].

reasons.correct: The answer correctly states that the first report covers a period of 2 weeks [S1, S6].

results.question: I'm 22 and have no vocational qualification. Do I have to apply for studies to get the benefit?
results.answer: Yes, if you are under 25 and do not have a vocational qualification or higher education degree, you must apply for admission to at least two education programmes that begin in the autumn term [S2][S5][S8]. You must also participate in any entrance exam you are invited to [S2][S8]. You should contact employment services to agree on these education applications in more detail [S2][S8].

results.question: Can I get my travel costs paid when I go to an aptitude test for labour market training?
results.answer:
Yes, as an unemployed jobseeker, you can apply for reimbursement of travel expenses when you travel to an aptitude test or admission event for labour market training [S1][S4]. 

The employment authority must consider the reimbursement appropriate for the availability of labour and your employment [S8]. Your trip is calculated starting from your actual place of residence [S8].

results.question: Kela paid me labour market subsidy before May 2026. Will they check my income now?
results.answer:
If Kela paid you basic unemployment allowance or labour market subsidy without applying a means test before you were transferred to the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026, Kela will check your income by 30 September 2026 [S2]. This is to see how much income must be taken into account in the means test [S2]. Once determined, your income will affect the next payment period of your benefit [S2].

Note: The labour market subsidy was abolished when Kela began paying the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026. [S9]

results.question: what is yleistuki
results.answer:
General social security benefit (yleistuki) is an unemployment benefit that Kela may pay you [S5].
It is intended for unemployed jobseekers who do not qualify for or have used up their earnings-related unemployment allowance [S2].
To get it, you must be 18–64 years old, live permanently in Finland, and be registered as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services [S5].
You can get the general social security benefit only if you are available for work on the labour market [S6].
